quickTips.tip3: Mention sleeved cards as a positive

likeNew.label: Like New
likeNew.fullDescription: Opened but essentially untouched. This game looks like you just removed the shrink wrap. Many games get opened, admired, and put on the shelf - if that's your game, this is probably the right grade.
boxCriteria: No visible wear, scuffs, or scratches
No shelf wear or storage marks
componentCriteria: All components present and accounted for
Cards show no wear - edges crisp, no bowing
Tokens unpunched, or punched with no damage
likeNew.proTip: If you've played even once or twice, consider Very Good instead. Like New means essentially untouched.

veryGood.label: Very Good
veryGood.fullDescription: Played and enjoyed, but handled with care. A game in Very Good condition is what you'd happily give as a gift.
boxCriteria: Minor shelf wear or light scuffing
No tears, splits, or structural damage
componentCriteria: Cards show minimal handling - light edge wear at most
Tokens punched cleanly, no lifting or tearing
veryGood.proTip: This is the sweet spot for most second-hand games. Buyers get a great game at a fair price.

good.label: Good
good.fullDescription: Clearly pre-loved - this game has seen regular play but remains fully functional. All the adventures, some of the wear.
boxCriteria: Corner wear - soft corners, possible minor splits
Light ring wear or sticker residue
componentCriteria: All components present (or missing pieces clearly noted)
Cards show shuffling wear on edges
Boards may have minor warping or edge wear
good.proTip: Many collectors are happy with Good condition for games they want to play rather than display.

acceptable.label: Acceptable
acceptable.fullDescription: Well-loved and showing it. This game works, but it's seen better days. Always note what's missing or damaged in your listing description - buyers deserve to know exactly what they're getting.
boxCriteria: Corner splits, tears, or tape repairs
componentCriteria: All crucial components present (minor pieces may be missing)
Cards worn - may need sleeves to play comfortably
Boards may have noticeable wear or warping
acceptable.proTip: Be very specific about damage. 'Acceptable with taped corner' is better than vague descriptions.

punchedTokens.title: Punched vs unpunched tokens
punchedTokens.description: Whether cardboard tokens have been punched from their sheets matters to some buyers.
details: Unpunched: tokens still in their original sheets
Cleanly punched: removed carefully with no damage

sleevedCards.title: Sleeved cards
sleevedCards.description: Cards protected in sleeves are a plus. Note this in your listing.

paintedMinis.title: Painted miniatures
paintedMinis.description: Some buyers want painted minis, others don't. Be clear about the state.

philosophy.title: When you're unsure
philosophy.content: If you're debating between two grades, go with the lower one. A buyer who receives a game in better condition than expected is delighted.

intro.title: Condition grading guide

quickReferenceTable.disclaimer: Value percentages are rough guidelines. Rare and out-of-print games often sell for more regardless of condition.

punchedTokens.title: Punched vs unpunched tokens
punchedTokens.description: Whether cardboard tokens have been punched from their sheets matters to some buyers.
details: Unpunched: tokens still in their original sheets, never removed
Punched: tokens removed from sheets (standard for any played game)
Cleanly punched: removed carefully with no lifting, tearing, or damage
Roughly punched: some lifting, tearing, or white edges visible

sleevedCards.title: Sleeved cards
sleevedCards.description: Cards protected in sleeves are a plus. Note this in your listing.
details: Cards sleeved since purchase (never shuffled unsleeved)
Cards sleeved after some play (mention any pre-sleeve wear)
Note if sleeves are included or if cards will be removed from sleeves

paintedMinis.title: Painted miniatures
paintedMinis.description: Some buyers want painted minis, others specifically don't. Be clear about the state.
details: Fully painted (describe quality: tabletop standard, display quality, etc.)

promosExtras.title: Promos & extras
promosExtras.description: Promotional content, Kickstarter extras, or expansion material adds value - make sure buyers know.
details: Note if from Kickstarter or retail edition
Mention any bonus components not in retail version
Separate pricing for valuable promos is acceptable

editionLanguage.title: Edition & language
editionLanguage.description: Edition matters a lot. Different editions can have different components, art, or rules.

listingTips.likeNew: Opened to read the rules, never played. All components still in original packaging. Cards never shuffled. Stored flat on a shelf in a smoke-free home.
listingTips.veryGood: Played maybe five times. Cards sleeved from first play, no wear. All components present. Original insert intact. Box shows minor shelf wear.
listingTips.good: Box shows shelf wear and one soft corner. Inside is in great shape - cards show light edge wear from shuffling. All components present.
listingTips.acceptable: Box has significant wear and a taped corner. Components are all there and play fine, but cards show shuffling wear. Rulebook has some creases. Good candidate for sleeving.

photoTips.intro: Good photos build trust. Here's what to show:
photoTips.tip: Natural daylight works best. Photograph on a plain background and show actual condition, not the best angle.

boxFront.title: Box front
boxFront.description: Straight on, good lighting - shows the game and any wear

boxBack.title: Box back
boxBack.description: Shows edition info and component list

boxCorners.title: Box corners
boxCorners.description: If there's wear, show it honestly

componentsSpread.title: Components spread
componentsSpread.description: Show what's included - full component photo

anyDamage.title: Any damage
anyDamage.description: Close-ups of specific issues buyers should know about

cards.title: Cards
cards.description: Show edge wear if present - that's where wear shows first

commonMistakes.mistake: "It's old, so it must be worn"
commonMistakes.correction: Age doesn't equal condition. A 20-year-old game stored well can be Like New. A 2-year-old game from 50 game nights might be Good.
It matters to collectors. Many buyers care about box condition for display. Grade it honestly.
Complete also means original. If you've replaced dice or printed new player aids, note it.
Stick to our four grades: Like New, Very Good, Good, Acceptable. Custom terms make comparison harder.

commonMistakes.mistake: Grading based on how much you paid
commonMistakes.correction: A €100 game in rough shape is still Acceptable. Grade the actual condition, not the value.

philosophy.title: When you're unsure
philosophy.content: If you're debating between two grades, go with the lower one. A buyer who receives a game in better condition than expected is delighted. A buyer who receives a game in worse condition than expected opens a dispute. Under-promise, over-deliver.
